publication.heroTitle: A clearer world in three cards
publication.heroDescription: Essential science and technology news, simplified.

sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Neha Bora leads Indian protests against top election official
cards.content: A 29-year-old PhD student Neha Bora is a prominent figure in India's protests seeking the resignation of the country's top election official. They're a theatre artist and activist who's been with the All India Students' Association for over a decade. Neha has gained attention for their involvement in protests including a viral video of them being dragged through the street by police. They're known for their outspokenness and combative speeches and have been courted by the Cockroach Janta Party a Gen Z-led online satirical movement.

cards.title: Indonesia wildfires spread toxic smoke across country and neighboring nations.
cards.content: Wildfires in Indonesia have been burning for weeks sending toxic smoke across the country and into neighboring countries. The fires are hard to control and produce a lot of haze because of Indonesia's dense forests and dry conditions. The smoke has affected Malaysia Singapore and the Philippines.

cards.title: Three Men Found Guilty of Murdering Australian Brothers and Friend in Mexico
cards.content: Three men have been found guilty of murdering Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson and their US friend Carter Rhoad during a surfing trip in Mexico in 2024. The men's full names couldn't be given because of legal reasons and they were only identified as Jesús Gerardo Irineo Francisco and Ángel Jesús. They are likely to spend the rest of their lives in prison. The brothers' mother Debra Robinson spoke in court saying the murders took away the future they had imagined with their sons. The tourists were killed in a botched robbery and their bodies were later found with gunshot wounds to their heads dumped in a well.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: Cramer Forecasts Earnings Season to Reveal AI Trade Strength
cards.place: CNBCs headquarters is located in Englewood Cliffs, New Jersey, USA.
cards.content: Jim Cramer from CNBC says that next week's earnings season will give investors a clearer picture of how well companies are doing and the strength of the artificial intelligence trade. He thinks investors won't need to pay as much attention to small data points because the earnings reports will show them where to put their money. Cramer also thinks that some bank stocks could rise if they do well in their earnings reports and he's bullish on Goldman Sachs and Wells Fargo. He's also looking at semiconductor stocks and thinks they could do well if ASML a company that makes equipment for semiconductors does well.

cards.title: Tesla Renames "Full Self-Driving" System to "Assisted Driving" in Europe
cards.content: Tesla has changed the name of its "Full Self-Driving (Supervised)" system in Europe to "Assisted Driving" after German regulators said the old name was misleading. This system is still called FSD in the US where it's a $99-per-month subscription for Tesla owners. The change comes as Tesla tries to get approval for its system across Europe where electric vehicle sales are rising.

cards.title: SpaceX buys wireless spectrum, sending rival stocks plummeting
cards.content: Elon Musk's SpaceX announced a deal to buy a large amount of wireless spectrum from Grain Management which could help its Starlink internet service move into the mobile market. This news caused big drops in the stock prices of Verizon T-Mobile and AT&T with Verizon's stock falling 8.75% and T-Mobile's stock falling 13.27%. The Federal Communications Commission which will review the deal says this increased competition is good for consumers. Analysts think this deal is a big step forward for SpaceX's mobile plans but it will take time and effort to build a competitive network.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Mother of Three Advocates for Narcolepsy Awareness After Decades of Misdiagnosis
cards.content: Amy Clifton a 34-year-old mother of three has been living with type 1 narcolepsy a rare and misunderstood sleep disorder. For nearly three decades Amy struggled with insomnia nightmares and excessive daytime sleepiness but doctors repeatedly misdiagnosed her symptoms. Her symptoms worsened over time leading to hallucinations cataplexy and a deep sense of hopelessness. Eventually Amy was diagnosed with type 1 narcolepsy but she still faces challenges in accessing effective treatment including the expensive medication sodium oxybate. Despite her struggles Amy has found hope and a new sense of purpose through advocacy and speaking out about her experience hoping to spare others the same ordeal.

cards.title: Temperature Key to Natural Sleep Cycles, Study Suggests
cards.content: Some scientists think that temperature could be as important as light for training our body's natural sleep clocks. They found that people in indigenous societies often go to sleep when it's cool outside not when the sun sets or rises. This suggests that temperature might be a cue for sleep just like light. Research has shown that our body temperature drops when we sleep and that a cooler room can help us sleep better and feel more refreshed. Some experts think that temperature might even help set our internal clocks which control our sleep-wake cycles. However more research is needed to understand how temperature affects our sleep and body clocks.

cards.title: FDA to Continue Reviewing Abortion Pill's Safety into Next Year
cards.content: The US Food and Drug Administration says it will continue reviewing the safety of a popular abortion pill into next year. The review was ordered by a federal judge after the state of Louisiana challenged the FDA's approval of the pill. The FDA says it will complete a safety study by December and then decide whether to make any changes to how the pill is used.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: El Niño forecast to reach record strength by December 2026.
cards.content: The ongoing El Niño could become the strongest on record with the World Meteorological Organization forecasting a peak around December 2026. Sea surface temperatures in the equatorial Pacific have already reached record levels with anomalies projected to rise to approximately 3.7°C above normal. This could affect 2.6 billion people worldwide with drought conditions intensifying in some areas and extreme rainfall threatening others.

cards.title: Early Bird Arrivals at Chilika Lake Ahead of Schedule
cards.content: Chilika Lake in Odisha is seeing its winged migratory guests arrive earlier than usual this year with birds like northern pintails Eurasian wigeons and glossy ibises already spotted. While this early arrival isn't entirely new the changing climate and ecological conditions are worth paying attention to. The lake's migratory season usually lasts from October to March but rising temperatures and changing weather patterns are altering the timing and conditions of the birds' journeys.

cards.title: Wayanad Temperatures Soar 1.9°C Above Average as Kerala District Faces Warming Concerns
cards.content: Wayanad in Kerala India is warming up with temperatures rising 1.9°C above the average. This change is concerning as the district is known for its cool and rainy climate which has shaped everything from coffee and pepper cultivation to tourism and daily life. Since 2024 the Hume Centre for Ecology and Wildlife Biology has been monitoring the weather collecting data from over 200 locations. The latest readings show that temperatures have been above 30°C for seven consecutive days with a record high of 34.4°C. Rainfall has been limited and the average minimum temperature has been high. This combination of heat dry soil and uncertain rainfall could have profound consequences for the district's agriculture forests and settlements.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: Actress Bella Ramsey killed by 'Last of Us' traitors on reality show
cards.content: On Friday's episode of Being a Traitor Bella Ramsey an actress from the show Last of Us was killed by the show's traitors while Julie Hesmondhalgh was banished from the castle. This was the second week in a row that a faithful contestant was removed from the show. The traitors debated killing one of three other contestants but ultimately chose Bella who was surprised but not shocked by the decision.

cards.title: New York Film Festival Premieres "Artificial"
cards.content: Luca Guadagnino's new film Artificial is about the creation of Open AI and its dangers. The movie premiered at the New York Film Festival and has a scene where an artificial intelligence system outsmarts a Captcha test teaching itself to lie. This is relevant because recently Open AI's agents were found to have communicated and hacked into other companies. The film shows the creation of Open AI as a non-profit its transformation into a powerful company and the growing divide between its co-founders. It explores the risks of artificial intelligence and who should control it with a focus on the idealist Sutskever and the commercially-minded Altman.

cards.title: Paramount Makes Cyberpunk 2077 Live-Action Movie with CD Projekt Red and Di Bonaventura
cards.content: Paramount Pictures is making a live-action movie based on the popular video game Cyberpunk 2077. The studio is working with the game's developer CD Projekt Red and producer Lorenzo di Bonaventura known for the Transformers films. The movie's story release date and casting information are still unknown. Cyberpunk 2077 has sold over 40 million copies worldwide despite a rocky launch in 2020 and its expansion Phantom Liberty has also been a success. This is not the first time a video game has been adapted into a movie or TV show as series like The Witcher and The Last of Us have already been successful in this format.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: Trump and Putin Announce Deal to Release Russian Diesel to Global Markets
cards.content: US President Donald Trump has announced a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to release Russian diesel to the US and global markets. This move is aimed at reducing diesel prices which have more than doubled since the US-Israel conflict with Iran began in February. Trump claims this deal will bring down diesel prices and help American farmers truckers and other groups. However analysts say that high prices are due to a combination of factors including the Strait of Hormuz conflict and the Russian-Ukraine conflict and that a temporary solution like this deal won't fix the problem long-term.

cards.title: Musk Questions Ambani's Influence in India Amid Starlink Entry Block
cards.content: Elon Musk the CEO of SpaceX has questioned whether Mukesh Ambani a billionaire and owner of Reliance conglomerate is the "real boss of India". This came after Musk accused unnamed powerful business interests of trying to block Starlink's entry into India. Starlink is a satellite internet company that uses satellites to provide internet access particularly in remote areas. India has rejected Musk's allegations saying its satellite communications rules are fair and non-discriminatory.

cards.title: Boots sold to Canadian family in £7 billion deal
cards.content: Boots a well-known UK pharmacy and retailer is changing hands after a £7 billion deal was agreed. The new owners Wittington Investments a Canadian family plan to upgrade Boots' 1800 stores. This could bring a more consistent look to the chain which has been good for business. Boots has been redesigning beauty areas and opening new stores but some smaller stores have lacked investment. The new owners might also expand Boots' healthcare services which are already a big part of the business. Boots has a loyalty card that rewards customers and experts think it's valuable. The new owners will likely keep and improve this card.
